meta.source: FRED keyless CSV (BEA, BLS, Fed, BIS, Treasury); gold via Yahoo Finance
meta.note: A rules-based reading of Ray Dalio's framework (the economic machine, the growth/inflation quadrants, the short- and long-term debt cycles) applied to public data. It is an interpretation, not his own call.

forward.note: Each direction is a logistic regression on a leading-indicator score and the current 6-month momentum, refitted every January and tested only on months it had not seen. Where that model did worse out of sample than simple persistence (the last 6 months' direction continuing), persistence is used instead. Quadrant probabilities multiply the two, which assumes growth and inflation surprises are independent. Inputs are revised data, so real-time accuracy will be lower than the hit rates shown.

long_term.detail: Debt is shrinking relative to income because nominal growth (much of it inflation) is running above the interest rate on the debt, not because debt is being repaid.
warnings: Debt is still at the 91st percentile of its history (262% of GDP).
The 2025 deficit was 5.8% of GDP, against Dalio's 3% marker.

components.label: Debt / GDP vs history
components.note: Private + federal debt against every quarter since 1966. Higher = more leveraged.

components.label: Debt / GDP, 5-year change
components.note: +20pp in five years scores 1; flat scores 0.5; deleveraging scores below.

components.label: Federal interest / receipts vs history
components.note: The share of federal revenue that goes to interest before anything else is paid for, ranked against every quarter since 1947.

components.label: Effective rate minus nominal growth
components.note: When the rate paid on debt exceeds income growth, debt/income rises on its own. +2pp scores 1.

components.label: Federal deficit vs Dalio's 3% marker
components.note: 3% of GDP scores 0.3; every 5pp above it adds 1.

components.label: Foreign share of federal debt, 5y change
components.note: Falling foreign demand means more debt must be absorbed at home, or by the central bank.

components.label: Room to cut vs a typical recession
components.note: Fed funds divided by the median cut past recessions needed. 1x or more scores 0.

short_term.detail: Credit is growing and policy is steady.

policy.lever_detail: Rates could fall 3.9pp, short of the 5.8pp a typical recession has needed. A deep downturn would likely push the Fed back to balance-sheet tools.

productivity.read: Productivity is running near its long-run pace.

external.read: No external stress signal from the dollar, gold or foreign holdings.

outlook.headline: Inflationary boom now (borderline) · no clear lead for the next 6m
outlook.narrative: The economy reads as inflationary boom (growth flat, inflation rising) for 1 month(s) — borderline, since one axis is barely moving. Over the next 6 months the leading indicators give no clear lead: every quadrant sits between 23% and 27%. Long-term debt cycle: deleveraging via nominal growth, pressure 0.50 of 1. Short-term credit cycle: mid — steady. Policy lever: MP1 → MP2 — Rates could fall 3.9pp, short of the 5.8pp a typical recession has needed. A deep downturn would likely push the Fed back to balance-sheet tools.
risks: The deficit (5.8% of GDP) is well above Dalio's 3% marker.
Rate cuts alone may not be enough in a real downturn.

engine_compare.note: The engine answers 'how likely is a recession in the next year'. The Dalio lens answers 'which growth-and-inflation environment is coming, and how much room is left in the debt cycle'. Disagreement is information, not an error.
